title: General specialization slices test the ordinary nearby comparison
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a finite-type morphism of schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $\Lambda$ a finite commutative ring annihilated by an integer invertible on $S$, and $K\in D^b(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the vanishing topos, exact inverse images and ordinary comparison $\beta$ of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Choose geometric points $a,b$ of $S$ and a geometric specialization $b\to a$ [def-weil-geometric-point], represented by an $S$-map $S_{(b)}\to S_{(a)}$ between strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. Put $X_{(a)}=X\times_SS_{(a)}$, $X_{(b)}=X\times_SS_{(b)}$, $X_a=X\times_Sa$, and let $i_a:X_a\to X_{(a)}$ and $j_b:X_{(b)}\to X_{(a)}$ be the canonical maps. The specialization defines a geometric morphism $e_{a,b}:(X_a)_{\mathrm{Et}}\to V_f$, and there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$e_{a,b}^*R\Psi_fK\simeq i_a^*Rj_{b,*}(K|_{X_{(b)}}).$$
For any $g:T\to S$ and compatible specialization $b_T\to a_T$ above $b\to a$, let $h:X_{a_T}\to X_a$ be the fibre map, and write $i_{a_T},j_{b_T}$ for the analogous maps over $T$. The pullback along $e_{a_T,b_T}$ of the ordinary comparison for $g$ is identified with the ordinary sliced comparison
$$h^*i_a^*Rj_{b,*}(K|_{X_{(b)}})\longrightarrow i_{a_T}^*Rj_{b_T,*}(K_T|_{X_{T,(b_T)}}).$$
For any integer $r$, the ordinary comparison cone on $V_{f_T}$ has $\mathcal H^q=0$ for $q\le r$ if and only if, for every geometric specialization $b\to a$ of $S$ and every compatible specialization $b_T\to a_T$ above it (equivalently, every geometric specialization of $T$, with $b\to a$ its image in $S$), the sliced comparison cone on $X_{a_T}$ has $\mathcal H^q=0$ for $q\le r$; a single fixed pair $b\to a$ does not suffice. The assertion permits arbitrary $T$, and also holds after an arbitrary preliminary base change of $(f,K)$. The generic strict localization $S_{(b)}$ in these formulas is not replaced by the geometric point $b$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, p. 6, first proof paragraph and the first displayed sliced comparison; the pointwise explanation immediately below it. Author PDF read online; local archival PDF WANTED.

proof.text: First check the inputs after arbitrary base change. For any $u:U\to S$, put $X_U=X\times_SU$ and $K_U=u_X^*K$. By lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change (2), the projection $f_U:X_U\to U$ is of finite type, with no hypothesis on $u$ (affinewise: the finitely many generators of each chart algebra $B$ over $A$ still generate $B\otimes_AA'$ over $A'$, and quasi-compactness is preserved). The constant-coefficient inverse image is exact and termwise by the oriented-nearby-cycles definition. The exact-functor cohomology isomorphism gives $\mathcal H^q(K_U)=u_X^*\mathcal H^q(K)$, so the same finite interval bounds $K_U$. An integer killing $\Lambda$ still kills it, and its inverse on $S$ pulls back to an inverse on $U$. Consequently the specialization-slice lemma applies to $f,K$ and to every $f_U,K_U$, including $U=T$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, printed p. 6: first proof paragraph, sliced comparison and pointwise explanation; section 1, printed p. 2: strict-local Milnor tubes. The input checks are elementary from affine finite generation and exact inverse image; cohomology uses Stacks homology.tex Tag 010N (lemma-exact-functor).

proof.text: Since $D^b\subset D^+$, apply lem-trf-nearby-specialization-slice to $f,K$. Its specialization morphism is the required $e_{a,b}$, and its canonical isomorphism is exactly $e_{a,b}^*R\Psi_fK\simeq i_a^*Rj_{b,*}(K|_{X_{(b)}})$. Fix $g:T\to S$ and denote the induced map $V_{f_T}\to V_f$ by $v$. The compatibility clause of that same lemma, applied to the chosen compatible specialization over $T$, identifies $e_{a_T,b_T}^*(\beta_{g,K})$ with the displayed ordinary sliced comparison. In particular its source is $h^*i_a^*Rj_{b,*}(K|_{X_{(b)}})$ and its target is $i_{a_T}^*Rj_{b_T,*}(K_T|_{X_{T,(b_T)}})$. Here $\beta_{g,K}:v^*R\Psi_fK\to R\Psi_{f_T}K_T$ is the counit-mate comparison of the definition; no invertibility is used. The generic side in the cited lemma is the entire strict localization $S_{(b)}$, so there is no replacement by the geometric point $b$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, printed p. 6: first proof paragraph, sliced comparison and pointwise explanation; section 1, printed p. 2: strict-local Milnor tubes.

proof.text: Let $C_g$ be a cone of $\beta_{g,K}$ on $V_{f_T}$. For a slice $e=e_{a_T,b_T}$, its sheaf inverse image is exact by lem-trf-nearby-specialization-slice. Apply lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated to this exact functor between the abelian categories of constant-$\Lambda$-module sheaves. It carries the distinguished triangle defining $C_g$ to a distinguished triangle with first arrow $e^*\beta_{g,K}$; thus $e^*C_g$ is a cone of the sliced comparison from step 2. Concretely the cone convention in def-weil-abstract-derived-category has degree $q$ term $B^q\oplus A^{q+1}$ and differential $\left(\begin{smallmatrix}d_B&\alpha\\0&-d_A\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. The additive termwise inverse image preserves this direct sum and this differential, giving precisely the cone for $e^*\alpha$, with no degree shift or truncation change. The conclusion concerns the isomorphism class of each cone; it does not require a functorial choice of cones in the derived category.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), termwise exact functor; definition-cone and definition-distinguished-triangle, cone convention as in def-weil-abstract-derived-category.

proof.text: Apply the cohomology-vanishing clause of lem-trf-nearby-specialization-slice to $f_T$ and $A=C_g$. It says that $\mathcal H^q(C_g)=0$ for every $q\le r$ if and only if $\mathcal H^q(e_{a_T,b_T}^*C_g)=0$ for every $q\le r$ and every geometric specialization slice over $T$. By step 3 these are exactly the sliced comparison cones in the statement. All specializations over $T$ occur: take $(a,b)$ to be their images over $S$. The quantifier here ranges over all such choices of $(a,b)$ as well; it does not keep one specialization of $S$ fixed. This proves both implications with the same integer $r$, including negative $r$. The cited lemma imposes no Noetherian or finite-type condition on $T$. Finally start instead with any $U\to S$ and $(f_U,K_U)$: step 1 verifies the inputs, and the successive-base-change compatibility in the cited lemma identifies the comparison maps used in steps 2--3 with those of this new pair. The identical cone argument proves the assertion after every preliminary base change.

The coefficient category is the same in both nodes: D(Mod Λ_X) on the small étale site, and the item's D^b lies inside the node's D^+. β is the counit mate, as in ILO 1.9/4.3. The item is a corollary of the existing same-unit lem-trf-nearby-specialization-slice. The split uses that node's statement clauses (slice isomorphism, compatibility over T, exact e^*, detection of H^{≤r}) and adds a correct cone passage. For the cone, e^*C(α)=C(e^*α) termwise by lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated, with no shift. There are no new nodes, no cycle (checked by traversal), no duplicates beyond the reused general node, no SGA source and no tool_uses. Two repairs are in fixes/: (1) C1/E5: step 1 only argued finite type for an affine open of U that maps into an affine open of S; it now cites the Mathlib leaf lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change (2), with proof_deps updated. (2) B2/E3: the statement's sentence 'every such sliced comparison cone', after choosing a fixed b→a, can be read with b→a fixed. That reading is false, since slices above one pair are not conservative on V_{f_T}. I rewrote the sentence to quantify over every specialization b→a of S and every compatible b_T→a_T, writing 𝓗^q. This is the reading the proof and the citer use, so it is a clarification, not a weakening. Small cases checked: X=∅, Λ=0, T=∅, g=id, punctual S, strictly henselian trait, negative r.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
